Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 1 6:17: and receive every person with joy, even if he is your enemy, for through this he will turn into a friend, and the merit is yours. Let all your words be gentle and spoken in a low voice, and do not cross over into the territory of anger. Remove sadness and worry from your heart, and put away evil from your flesh, for it is a snare for you, removing the Holy Spirit from you. And flee from positions of authority, which shorten your years.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 1 6:18: And distance yourself from idle talk, from falsehood, from flattery, from mockery, and from evil speech, for these are among the classes that will never receive the presence of the Shechinah in the World to Come. Grasp hold of humility, which brings one to the Holy Spirit, and be like a threshold trodden upon by great and small alike. Stop up your ears from hearing gossip and evil speech, and be like a mute, opening your mouth only for Torah, for the commandments, and for necessary business dealings, and receive people with a pleasant countenance and a gentle tongue, and do not praise yourself for your good deeds before others, for you will lose your reward, and you will even be punished for it:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 1 6:19: Afterward, be very careful with the afternoon (Minchah) prayer, for Elijah, of blessed memory, was answered only through the Minchah prayer (Berachot 6b), and moreover it is a time of strict judgment, for "the day has turned" and "the shadows of evening are stretched out." And be even more careful with the evening (Ma'ariv) prayer, for by then darkness has already covered the earth and all the harmful forces are stirred to encamp upon a person's body and soul as it ascends to render its account to its Maker.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 1 6:20: There are other things I have written in Gate Five; see there — and for the sake of brevity I have not repeated them here:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 1 6:21: Now let us establish a comprehensive remedy to be saved from all the ailments of the soul, which are three things, since the essential source of a person's errors and self-inflicted damage is three things: the first, that the material nature makes a person forget the good [he received], leading him to sin; the second, that he tells himself there is some advantage on a good day to remaining in that good; the third, that even if he does set his mind to remember, he will act with even greater deliberateness, saying to himself, "What shall we eat during the seventy years of our lives?" — and this is worse than the first two:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 1 6:22: Therefore, my son, do this and save yourself from these three transgressions of Israel. Against the first, keep it constantly before your eyes: do not act hastily in doing anything or in saying any careless word, but be deliberate, deliberate in your mind about whether to do or say something, or to refrain, for the fruit of haste is regret, and there is no way afterward to restore the matter to its sheath.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 1 6:23: And against the second, set the fear of the Lord before your face; let the fear of the day of death and being brought down to the grave never depart from before your eyes — until the body rots, is turned over for further rotting, is eaten by worms, and the punishment of chibut hakever (the beating of the grave), the judgment of Gehinnom, and the great day of judgment for all who come into the world — for even Samuel, who was equal in weight to Moses and Aaron, feared it (Chagigah 4b):
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 1 6:24: And against the third, let him truly acquire the trait of trust, that His eyes are upon all a man's ways, to give him according to his ways, and that neither his deeds nor his stratagems can raise or lower his fortune at all, for the race is not to the swift, and let him cast his burden upon Him, as it is said (in the Rosh Hashanah liturgy), "Happy is the man who does not forget You, and the son of man who strengthens himself in You, for those who seek You shall never stumble, nor shall those who trust in You ever be put to shame."
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 1 6:25: Thus far shall suffice the discourses necessary for the conduct of a person to be a tzaddik or a chasid; from here on we shall occupy ourselves with words of rebuke to subdue a person, and with making known the punishment that comes upon a person who stands on a bad path, and with making known the tremendous reward that comes to him, if he desires greatly his Torah and his commandments:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 1:1-4: And now, son of man, open your eyes from blindness and see that all the pleasures and good things of this world are vanity, mere illusions and delusions. Why should you exalt yourself over other people? If it is because of your upright stature — everyone was created in the image of God like you. If it is because of your lineage — we are all children of one man, we are all children of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. If it is because of wealth — how many worthless and reckless people are richer than you? And moreover, the Lord makes poor and makes rich, and let not the rich man glory in his riches, for perhaps wealth is stored up for its owner to his own hurt.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 1:5: And if because of authority and honor — how many people of despised lineage rule over the world, as it is written (Proverbs 30:22), "a slave when he becomes king"; and moreover, wealth and honor come from before Him, and it is He who humbles the proud to the ground. And if because of wisdom — how many great sages have been banished from this world and from the World to Come, as with Doeg, Achitophel, and Jeroboam; and it is in His power, blessed be He, "to remove speech from the trustworthy, and take away the sense of the elders" — let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, and how can you exalt yourself, when your beginning was from a putrid drop, and you entered and departed through the passage of urine?
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 1:6: You are shame and disgrace in your lifetime, maggot and worm in your death, and though you are dust, and to dust you shall return, and become as though you never were: how then can you be angry at another when you should be angry at yourself, for you yourself tear at your own soul in your anger and worship idolatry in your anger, and you anger your Maker and are destined to be punished for it,
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 1:7: and how can you take offense at the vanities of this world, when your end is to die, and a spirit passes over it and it is no more, and its place shall no longer recognize it, and those who saw it shall say, 'Where is it?' And how can you grieve over a world that is not yours, and yet not grieve over the separation of your soul from your body, in trembling and shuddering and a dark dread falling upon it,
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 1:8: and how can you covet to amass gold and to build houses and spacious upper chambers, when your end is a grave a cubit by a cubit, a cubit high beneath the earth, and you take nothing with you, and you leave your wealth to others; and why do you labor to become rich when everything depends on one's fated fortune, even a Torah scroll in the ark; and why should you grieve over a world that is not yours, when in the blink of an eye you go to another world, and everything you labored for turns to nothing, to emptiness, and to vanity, and your strength is spent for naught; and why should you despise the Torah of life, the life eternal, in order to accumulate money, a life of but a passing moment, when everything God has decreed for you — whether poor or rich — cannot be added to and cannot be subtracted from, for the Lord makes poor and makes rich; and you have lost your world, the world of life, while only half your desire came to your hand; and why should you take pleasure in delicacies, when tomorrow your bones will be laid bare upon the dust, a worm spread beneath you and a maggot your covering; and how can you seek authority and lofty rank, when man's hope is but a worm?
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 1:9: And moreover, one kingdom does not encroach upon another by even a hair's breadth, for sovereignty belongs to the Lord, and it is in His hand to raise up and to strengthen anyone, and He humbles even the exalted; and how can you speak evil speech of your fellow who is better than you, when so many prosecuting angels recount your own wrongdoing and mention your sins before Him who spoke and the world came into being?
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 1:10: And why should you hate your enemies, when you have no greater enemy than yourself — you bring evil upon yourself, torment and afflict your eternal soul, and give delight to your body, a worm and a clod of transient, perishable earth; why do you love your enemy — he is the evil inclination within you, seeking your harm, watching you in order to bring about your death; and, like a bird hastening into a snare, he pierces his own liver with an arrow, not knowing it is at the cost of his own life:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 1:11: And how can you flatter and feel shame before one born of woman like yourself, and not feel shame before the mighty, awesome, and terrible King, who judges the whole earth, whose glory fills the whole earth, in whose hand is the soul of every living thing, who from His dwelling place watches over all the inhabitants of the earth? And how can you sin in secret, when all your deeds and words are written in a book, for His eyes range over the ways of man throughout the whole earth, and He counts all your steps, and for all these things God will bring you into judgment for everything hidden; and how can you waste your time on things that pass away and perish, when time is short and when will you provide for your eternal home — for whoever does not prepare on the eve of the Sabbath will not eat on the Sabbath:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 1:12: Look and see how many have died in their youth, how many stillborn infants and nursing babes have perished and come to nothing, withering like the top of a grain-stalk, for man does not know his own time, when he will die and his name be lost; and how can you forget the day of death, the judgment of the grave, the judgment of Gehinnom, and the great and awesome day of judgment — who can bear it, yet you have hidden your eyes from them? There is nothing more inevitable than this, for no man is redeemed from the grave, and you will groan in your latter end, when the gates of repentance will already be locked before you, and no remedy will avail for your wound and your iniquities,
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 1:13: and how can you avert your eyes from death, when it is coiled like a serpent at your heel, and every night you are like one dead, lying upon your bed, to remind you of the true death, and death is bound like tefillin between your eyes, like a slumber upon your eyelids; as you lie down it watches over you, and when you awaken you turn your eyes away from it, and gaze instead at the vanities of the world, at money that is not yours, at pleasures that are not yours, at authority that is not yours, and at a world that is not yours:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 2:1-3: On rebukes found in the words of our Sages, of blessed memory:

And these are they: A person should always (Eliyahu Rabbah, end of ch. 21) be one who fears Heaven in private just as in public. Happy is one who directs all his words and all his ways toward Heaven. Let your eyes and your heart always be with your Creator, so that you may be saved from every kind of sin and iniquity. Let the fear of your Maker always be upon you, and His awe upon your heart, upon your head, and before your eyes, and never remove them from your eyes, even for a single moment,
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 2:4: Let the day of death, the day of the grave, and the great day of judgment never depart from your eyes, as though you were seeing it, as though you were standing before it, as though you were entering into judgment — so that thoughts of sin, of which all your limbs bear witness against you, should not arise in your heart, for you are inevitably destined to give an account before the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He,
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 2:5: Every day one should say: Woe is me, for the day has passed and I have not done charity together with Torah study, for every day that has passed will never return to you:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 2:6: They said: at the hour a person departs from the world, the Angel of Death asks him: Did you occupy yourself with Torah and with acts of loving-kindness, and did you proclaim the sovereignty of your Maker morning and evening, and did you accept your fellow with a pleasant demeanor? If he has these things, his soul departs with a kiss; if not, and so on:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 2:7: The second judgment is the judgment of the grave. The day of the grave is harder than the judgment of Gehinnom, and even completely righteous people who did not sin are judged by it. And what can a person do to be saved from chibut hakever (the beating of the grave)? He should occupy himself with Torah, and love charity and rebuke and acts of loving-kindness, and bring Torah scholars and guests into his home and benefit them from his possessions, and pray his prayer with intention, and then he will be saved from chibut hakever, and will not even see the judgment of Gehinnom at all:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 2:8: The third judgment is the judgment of Gehinnom. At the time of judgment, the Holy One, blessed be He, asks him: Did you occupy yourself with Torah and with acts of loving-kindness? If he has these things, they exempt him from the judgment of Gehinnom, and so on. Happy is the person who makes himself like an ox to the yoke and like a donkey to its burden, and sits and reads and reviews words of Torah continually every day, and reads Torah, Prophets, and Writings, and reviews halachot and midrash, increasing time spent in study and decreasing time spent in commerce — immediately the Holy Spirit rests upon him, and so on:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 2:9: Elijah, our father, of blessed memory, said (Eliyahu Rabbah 9): I call heaven and earth to witness for me: whether man or woman, whether gentile or Jew, whether slave or maidservant — according to a person's deeds, so does the Holy Spirit rest upon him. Happy is one who keeps all these things constantly before him, and merits to complete them all the days of his life and to spend himself in them all the days of his life through all these deeds, provided that he guards himself, his limbs, and his body from every sin and iniquity — he merits all the honor stored up for the righteous, beyond number and measure, which no eye can see and no ear can hear, the honor prepared for the tzaddikim and the chasidim, as it is said (Isaiah 64:3), "and from of old they have not heard, nor perceived by the ear; no eye has seen a God besides You, who acts for those who wait for Him."
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 3:1-3: On the reward for fulfilling the Torah and its commandments:

And so that you may know the reason for performing the commandments at their root, as I have opened your ear in the First Part, I shall write you what is said in Sefer HaTikkunim, Tikkun 18 (32a) and Tikkun 70 (130a), and I shall glean their essentials and arrange them in the utmost brevity:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 3:4: Every prophet and every human being, each one ascends to his own particular limb, from which his soul was hewn, at the very head of the King; some in the hair follicles, in the eyes, in the ears, in the face, in the nose, in the mouth, in the neck, in the hands, in the stature that is the body, in the thighs, in the loins, in the legs, in the sign of the covenant, in the brain, in the heart. And every one of these limbs has its own known sefirah among the ten sefirot, and all these limbs are in the image of the King's body, and there is one whose soul comes from the King's very garments:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 3:5: And all 613 commandments of the Torah are dependent on these limbs of the King's body. There are commandments dependent on the King's head, and there are those dependent on the eyes, and so on; and every commandment that rests upon each and every limb has its own known Name, and within it is the Name Havayah, which is the soul of that limb, and all the limbs are called appellations for the Name Havayah, which is within every limb; and every name and appellation of every limb has power only over its own limb, but the Holy One, blessed be He — the Name Havayah — has power in every place, like a soul whose power extends over every limb, and this is [the meaning of] "the whole earth is full of His glory."
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 3:6: And all commandments that a person performs not in order to receive reward depend upon the image of the King in the World of Atzilut, but commandments performed in order to receive reward depend upon the image of that which is called "the youth" above.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 3:7: And upon every limb of the King's image depend several angels, called "the eyes of the Lord," "the ears of the Lord," "the hands of the Lord," and so on, and all of them depend from the King's body like hair follicles that hang from the head:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 3:8: and every hair-follicle is one angel, and the 613 limbs of a person are all arranged according to the order of Creation; and for this reason a person is called "a small world." And through every commandment a person performs, he causes the Holy One, blessed be He, to be crowned as King over that limb of his soul corresponding to that commandment, and every limb of the soul is called by the name of that limb of the person's soul according to that commandment. And every limb of the soul is called a "candle," as it is written, "the candle of the Lord is the soul of man"; through it he performs that commandment, which is likewise called a candle, as it is written (Proverbs 20:24), "for the commandment is a candle."
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 3:9: A person needs to remove from every one of his limbs all evil, defiling thoughts and imaginings, which are the kelipot that dwell within him, and to prepare a pure and clean place for the Holy One, blessed be He, to dwell there — for any limb that is blemished through the sin a person commits, the Holy One, blessed be He, does not rest within that limb, as it is written, "for any man in whom there is a blemish shall not draw near," and whoever blemishes even one commandment, it is as though he has committed treason against the image of the King. He must burn away those kelipot that dwell there, among those commandments that dwell upon each and every limb, and remove them, since they are called "leaven" and "chametz," through these candles, of which it is said, "for the commandment is a candle," and it is written, "the candle of the Lord is the soul of man, searching all the chambers of the innards." And when the Holy One, blessed be He — who is the Name Havayah, blessed be He — and His appellations, called His limbs, and the hosts of angels that depend from that limb, dwell there, they guard that limb from all bad ailments and kelipot that had dwelt there. There are commandments that depend, and so on — every commandment of fear and love depends on the brain and the heart; every commandment of walking depends on the legs, such as walking to the synagogue, to a circumcision, to accompany the dead to burial, or to any walking for the sake of a commandment; and those who stand in the standing position during the Amidah prayer, upon their two legs.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 3:10: The commandment of circumcision depends upon the tzaddik, who is the drawn bow of the sign of the covenant; the prayer with the eighteen blessings recited while bowing and kneeling depend upon the tzaddik who is the "life of the worlds"; the master of stature of the body who raises up the Shechinah in prayer through the Name Havayah, the four bowings in prayer depend on the middle pillar; the arm-tefillin, on the left arm.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 3:11: All commandments of action depend on the hands, such as giving charity and binding the tefillin, with the right hand upon the left; and charity to the Holy One, blessed be He, is ninety Amens, four Kedushot, one hundred blessings, five books of the Torah every day, [as in the verses] "you shall surely open," "you shall surely give," "you shall surely furnish him" — these are the ten kinds of gifts, and so on.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 3:12: Tzitzit on the shoulders; the delight of the Sabbath through eating and drinking, and the sacrificial offerings of eating and drinking to the Holy One, blessed be He, such as "My offering, My bread," and the prayers that correspond to sacrifices, and blessing the Holy One, blessed be He, for everything one eats and drinks after praying, and not before — all of these depend upon the neck.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 3:13: The commandment to learn and to teach, and prayers and voices and utterances that call to the Holy One, blessed be He, [such as] Shema Yisrael twice a day, and songs and praises and thanksgivings — all these depend upon the mouth; and likewise the blowing of the shofar with the breath blown through the mouth, that breath becoming a sound; all judgments depend upon the speech of the mouth, and likewise upon the eyes, as they said (Sanhedrin 4b), "a judge has only what his eyes see."
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 3:14: Sacrifices, which are a pleasing fragrance to the Lord, and the fragrant woods of Havdalah, depend upon the nose. The recitation of the Shema and the hearing of the shofar, and all commandments concerning which it is said "if he made it heard to his own ear, he has fulfilled his duty," depend upon the ears. Tefillin depend upon the head, and all the commandments are interlinked with one another.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 3:15: And in the Sefer HaZohar, Parashat Naso (124a): When a person performs a single commandment — no more — in fear and love of the Holy One, blessed be He, for the sake of that commandment, the ten sefirot rest upon him, and whoever fulfills one commandment properly, it is as though he fulfills all 248 positive commandments, for there is no commandment that is not included in all 248.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 3:16: [Translation — When a person appoints the Holy One, blessed be He, as King over every limb, this is reckoned as if he had appointed Him King over the whole world, for a person is called a small world. And permission has not been given to reveal the reward of the reasons for the commandments, so that a person not serve the Holy One, blessed be He, in order to receive reward. But come and see: that soul which is in the image of its Master, who fulfills all these His commandments — when it ascends above, all the hosts of angels that depend on these commandments, and all the corrections and encampments of the King's body, ascend with it, and when it descends they all descend with it; and it is the ladder of which it is said (Genesis 28:12), "and behold, the angels of God ascending and descending upon it," and a voice descends through all the heights of the heavens: "Give honor to the image of the King."]
